name: 2009 Prairie Avenue (Meyer): the brick stable on the alley, K12
aka: the stable behind the Meyer house, 2009 Prairie

function.note: Sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn draws a two-storey brick building on the alley behind 2009, uncrossed, and letters it GARAGE. GARAGE is the 1911 sheet's word and is not read as the 1904 use (the K12 kit's restriction no_1911_use_labels; T-1837 study ruling 11; the T-1842 census row s35-2009-rear, whose own note backcasts the envelope and reconstructs the use as a stable/coach house). This record builds it as the house's stable and coach house: a carriage bay, a loft with its hatch and hoist, stable sash, and no motor-garage part. The use is RECONSTRUCTED; no source read names a horse, a carriage or a motor car on this lot.

research_note: T-1938 refines the district draft (T-2352) in place under the same id onto the K12 coach-house kit, the third of the package's alley buildings on the east side of Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street, to leave the draft. The sheet census (census row s35-2009-rear, trace s35fp-2009-b2) carries the building into 1904; the draft rules now skip that row. Read afresh off the committed sheet 35 raster by median darkness profiles rather than taken from the draft's fitted rectangle (12.5 x 7.0 m): the sheet draws a building 13.89 m deep from the alley line and 8.47 m along it, its north wall on the 2005/2009 lot line under a double line lettered 17" WALL 16' HIGH (a 17-inch wall 16 feet high, running on west along the lot line), its south wall 0.44 m inside the line of 2011's alley building, a window mark on its alley wall, and the house's one-storey brick rear range drawn against its yard wall. This copy of the sheet is coarse (0.186 m a pixel), so every reading here carries about a pixel. Nothing read dates the building before the 1911 sheet; that it stood by 1904 is the census's carry-back, which the district draft already made. No picture of the alley behind the 2000 block is known to this project.

documented_range.note: The draft's claim, kept: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Nothing else read dates it, so the range claims the 1904 target and no more. TO is the last day of the year the sheet was published, the latest date anything here shows it standing; it is not a demolition date.

position.symbolic_location: 2009 S. position.note: The middle of the building's alley (east) wall at grade, read off the committed sheet 35 raster (chicago/reference/prairie-avenue/sanborn-1911-and-robinson-1886/sanborn_1911_vol3_sheet_35.jpg) at pixel (1170.96, 408.84): the alley line by a median darkness profile over rows 395-425 (peak at column 1170.96; the building's alley wall is drawn on it), halfway between the north wall line (row 386.06, a profile over columns 1105-1160) and the south wall line (row 431.62, the same columns), each peak refined by a parabola through the three highest samples. Carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_35_gcps.json): local E 1469.787, N -3507.423. The bearing is the parcel's (prairie_2009, data/street_grid/1904.json, -0.611 degrees, the draft's 179.389 less the half turn its plan frame took). The fit's own residual, 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of reading on this coarse copy, is all that is claimed. The draft had stood its corner 3.4 m north and 1.2 m west of this wall's middle, its fitted 12.5 x 7.0 m rectangle turned the other way.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; none reads a 1911 Sanborn sheet. This position is pixel (1170.96, 408.84) of the committed sheet 35 raster carried through the similarity in data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_35_gcps.json (local_e = a*px + b*py + c, local_n = d*px + e*py + f) plus the datum origin, and the note carries the pixel and the result so the sum can be recomputed by hand.

footprint.note: About the middle of the alley wall, u east (toward the alley, so the building lies at negative u) and v north. The sheet draws the building from the alley line (pixel column 1170.96) back to its west wall line (column 1096.21, a profile over rows 395-425): 74.75 pixels at the sheet's 0.185854 m a pixel, 13.893 m; and from its north wall line (row 386.06) to its south wall line (row 431.62): 45.56 pixels, 8.468 m along the alley. A plain rectangle: the sheet draws no step, wing or porch on it. The lines 2.2 and 2.4 pixels outside the north and south wall lines (rows 383.85 and 433.98) are the 17-inch wall on the lot line and the north wall of 2011's building, not this building's.

stories.note: '2' lettered in the building's north-east corner, under its north wall line. Built as the kit's carriage room (3.6 m) under a loft whose walls rise 2.7 m more to the eave, under a 30-degree roof (4.01 m from eave to ridge over the 13.89 m span); those heights are RECONSTRUCTED. No dormer: the sheet draws none and the kit builds none.

construction.note: Drawn pink, the sheet's colour for brick. The small figures written inside its north and south wall lines are too coarse on this copy to read as wall thicknesses; the kit builds its own 13-inch walls.

value.note: Everything but the plan, the two storeys, the brick and the window mark's place is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-2009-stable-1938. The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, the label GARAGE, the alley wall on the alley line, the north wall on the 2005/2009 lot line under the double line the sheet letters 17" WALL 16' HIGH, the south wall 0.44 m inside the next line south, which is the north wall of 2011's alley building, one of the key's window marks on the alley wall 3.83 m from the south wall, and the house's one-storey brick rear range (mayer_house_2009_prairie's rear_range) drawn against the yard wall from 2.87 m south of the north wall to the south wall. The alley is on the EAST, so the kit is turned to face it (alley_side east), not mirrored, so that its party wall stands at the south end, back to back with 2011's building, and the open gable faces north over 2005's open back lot; it carries no opening, as nothing on the sheet says the wall had any and the 16-foot wall stands along that line. On the alley wall, counted from the party wall's inner face: a man door with a loft sash over it, the mark as a stable sash with a loft sash over it, and a carriage bay (3.0 m clear) toward the north end with the loft hatch and hoist over it. On the yard wall only a door, counted from the gable end, in the 2.87 m the house's range leaves open; the rest of that wall stands behind the range, so it is blind. The roof is the kit's gable with the ridge along the alley at 30 degrees, the pitch 1612's 14.0 m deep stable takes, 4.01 m from eave to ridge over the 13.89 m span; no dormer and no ventilator, as the sheet draws none. No workyard: the house's range fills the yard behind the building. No ramp, stair, lean-to, wing or range of the kit's own: the sheet draws none.

coach_house.note: The building's dimensions are the footprint's (inferred, above); its openings, roof and loft are the kit's, laid out for this lot, and RECONSTRUCTED. See the value's own note for each choice and what bounds it.
